candidates.original_title: Iodine Deficiency and Schooling Attainment in Tanzania
candidates.description: Protection from iodine deficiency in utero, provided by iodized oil capsule distribution programs, increases educational attainment.
candidates.citation_sentence: Field, Robles, and Torero (2009, hereafter FRT) seek to shed light on this question by estimating the effect on educational attainment of iodized oil capsule (IOC) distribution programs launched in 1986 in Tanzania.
candidates.notes: Narrow replication exactly reproduces FRT's original specification and results using the original THBS 2000 data. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Iodine Deficiency and Schooling Attainment in Tanzania
candidates.description: Protection from iodine deficiency in utero, provided by iodized oil capsule distribution programs, increases educational attainment.
candidates.citation_sentence: Field, Robles, and Torero (2009, hereafter FRT) seek to shed light on this question by estimating the effect on educational attainment of iodized oil capsule (IOC) distribution programs launched in 1986 in Tanzania.
candidates.notes: Wide replication pools five surveys (almost 4x sample size) and uses improved multi-compartment treatment models; no significant effect found in any specification. Authors state 'no effect is found' and 'We find no empirical support for a causal link.' They hedge on whether an effect could exist given measurement error and power limitations. candidates.original_title: Iodine Deficiency and Schooling Attainment in Tanzania
candidates.description: Protection from iodine deficiency in utero increases educational attainment in Tanzania, with particularly large effects for girls.
candidates.citation_sentence: Field, Robles, and Torero (2009, American Economic Journal: Applied Economics 1, 140-169) find large increases in educational attainment caused by a reduction of fetal iodine deficiency following a set of iodine supplementation programs in Tanzania. We revisit the Tanzanian iodine programs with a narrow and wide replication of the study by Field et al.
candidates.notes: The narrow replication exactly reproduces the original results, although the paper also reports that the findings disappear under alternative specifications. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.citation_sentence: Field, Robles, and Torero (2009, American Economic Journal: Applied Economics 1, 140-169) find large increases in educational attainment caused by a reduction of fetal iodine deficiency following a set of iodine supplementation programs in Tanzania.
